 Nebraska Cornhuskers Nebraska Cornhuskers Taking a look at how different areas of the Nebraska Cornhuskers are trending, here is the Cornhusker Stalk Report for early November.

 Fan Trust: Down
--> Fan Trust: Down
 A third straight loss for Nebraska football tends to bring with it a certain feeling of doom and gloom. That loss also being the third straight fourth-quarter collapse puts things in a bigger conversation.
--> A third straight loss for Nebraska football tends to bring with it a certain feeling of doom and gloom. That loss also being the third straight fourth-quarter collapse puts things in a bigger conversation.
 How are the timeouts being used? Is the head coach meddling too much with his coordinators? What's going on with the play calling in the red zone?
--> How are the timeouts being used? Is the head coach meddling too much with his coordinators? What's going on with the play calling in the red zone?
 Nebraska Cornhuskers head coach Matt Rhule talks with a referee during a timeout in the fourth quarter against the Washington Huskies at Memorial Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Fans can be fickle, but when you're losing games and it doesn't look to be a talent issue, that makes every little action get questioned even harder. How the game goes at Illinois on Friday, let alone the way the rest of the season shakes out, will be a strong indicator of whether fan trust can rebound or will start to crater.

 While volleyball continues its domination (more on that later), football's fall 5-0 to 5-3 has many ready to move on. While that may be an annual refrain when the calendar flips to November of the past decade, there is extra weight this year.

 Amy Williams and Co. are coming off a fourth NCAA Tournament appearance in the past five years. Fred Hoiberg's group just got the program's first March Madness win in history, pushing through to the Sweet 16.
--> Amy Williams and Co. are coming off a fourth NCAA Tournament appearance in the past five years. Fred Hoiberg's group just got the program's first March Madness win in history, pushing through to the Sweet 16.
 The people crave basketball season. It is finally, happily here.

 Fan Behavior: Down
--> Fan Behavior: Down
 Being disgruntled is one thing. Being shameful is another.
--> Being disgruntled is one thing. Being shameful is another.
 Coaches' families hear much more than the public tends to know about. The fact that Matt Rhule brought it up on Monday says the pressure of the season has him wanting to make sure fans aren't taking it too far. That's beside the fact that no child deserves to be berated because of how their parent performs at their job, no matter how much money is being made.
--> Coaches' families hear much more than the public tends to know about. The fact that Matt Rhule brought it up on Monday says the pressure of the season has him wanting to make sure fans aren't taking it too far. That's beside the fact that no child deserves to be berated because of how their parent performs at their job, no matter how much money is being made.
 What Rhule did condone was the throwing of objects by upset fans, which happened Saturday night, late in the game against Washington.
--> What Rhule did condone was the throwing of objects by upset fans, which happened Saturday night, late in the game against Washington.
 "You guys gotta remember: I'm from New York and I'm from Philly," Rhule began. "I've coached at Temple, where you walk out to see which sections are open, which sections aren't. I'll take (fans throwing stuff) all day.
"Our fans, it's not even winning and losing; it's when the football looks right and it doesn't. If you throw three turnovers and you have penalties, they're going to be upset. I'm here for all of it."
--> "You guys gotta remember: I'm from New York and I'm from Philly," Rhule began. "I've coached at Temple, where you walk out to see which sections are open, which sections aren't. I'll take (fans throwing stuff) all day.
"Our fans, it's not even winning and losing; it's when the football looks right and it doesn't. If you throw three turnovers and you have penalties, they're going to be upset. I'm here for all of it."

His experience with Big Ten Conference teams goes back more than a decade, including time covering programs such as the Nebraska Cornhuskers, Oregon Ducks, and USC Trojans. He has contributed to Sports Illustrated since 2021. Kaleb has won multiple awards for his sports coverage from the Nebraska Broadcasters Association and Midwest Broadcast Journalists Association. Prior to working in sports journalism, Kaleb was a Division I athlete on the Southern Illinois University-Edwardsville Track and Field team where he discussed NCAA legislation as SIUE's representative to the Ohio Valley Conference Student-Athlete Advisory Committee.
